content.user_title: Filter and Prioritize Medicinal Chemistry Libraries
content.value_statement: Large compound libraries are difficult to assess consistently with multiple medicinal chemistry criteria. This skill combines established filters, alerts, constraints, and reports.
actual_capabilities: Applies established rules including Lipinski, Veber, CNS, Oprea, lead-like, and REOS criteria.
Screens molecules with common alerts, NIBR filters, Lilly demerits, and PAINS patterns.
Calculates Bertz, Whitlock, and Barone molecular complexity metrics.
Enforces configurable property limits for molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen bonding, and rotatable bonds.
Detects named chemical groups and custom structural patterns.
Processes CSV, TSV, SDF, and SMILES text files into CSV results and summary reports.
limitations: Requires Python and compatible medchem, datamol, pandas, RDKit, and tqdm packages.
Filtering rules are guidelines and do not predict efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, or clinical success.
Invalid molecular records are removed, so users must review input quality and rejected entries.
Using all CPU cores can consume substantial resources on shared systems.

use_cases.title: Triage a screening library
use_cases.description: Apply drug-likeness rules and structural alerts before selecting compounds for experimental screening.

use_cases.title: Compare lead candidates
use_cases.description: Evaluate lead-like properties, complexity, reactive groups, and filter failures across a focused series.

use_cases.title: Build a reproducible filter pipeline
use_cases.description: Process molecular files with documented thresholds and export detailed results for downstream analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Check one molecule
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this SMILES string with the Rule of Five and Veber criteria. Explain each pass or failure: [SMILES].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single compound

prompt_templates.title: Screen a small list
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen these SMILES for Rule of Five, PAINS, and common structural alerts. Return a concise table with failure reasons: [SMILES list].

prompt_templates.title: Design a library filter
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a filtering workflow for [input file] using [rules], [alerts], and [property limits]. Preserve identifiers and summarize exclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Define a staged prioritization strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design staged filters for [target class] and [modality]. Include broad triage, structural alerts, complexity, custom constraints, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Compare three compounds with Rule of Five and PAINS filters.
output: Compound B: fails Rule of Five because one property exceeds its threshold.
Compound C: passes Rule of Five but matches a PAINS pattern.

output_examples.output: Processed 2,500 valid molecules. 1,840 passed property rules, 210 matched structural alerts, and 1,520 passed every selected filter.

output_examples.input: Explain why a candidate was excluded.
output_examples.output: Candidate M-17 exceeded the selected complexity limit and matched a reactive-group alert. Review both results before removing it from consideration.

best_practices: Choose filters for the biological target, modality, administration route, and development stage.
Record thresholds, filter versions, excluded compounds, and failure reasons for reproducibility.
Review flagged molecules with medicinal chemistry expertise before making irreversible decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a passing result as proof of safety, efficacy, or developability.
Do not apply every available filter without considering project-specific chemical space.
Do not remove flagged compounds without checking false positives, prodrugs, natural products, and unusual modalities.

faq.question: Which molecular formats are supported?
faq.answer: The batch script accepts CSV, TSV, SDF, and text files containing one SMILES string per line.

faq.question: Which drug-likeness rules are available?
faq.answer: The documentation covers Lipinski, Veber, CNS, Oprea, lead-like, Rule of Three, REOS, drug, and Golden Triangle rules.

faq.question: Can the skill detect structural liabilities?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports common alerts, NIBR filters, Lilly demerits, PAINS patterns, and named chemical groups.

faq.question: Does passing every filter mean a compound will succeed?
faq.answer: No. These filters provide prioritization signals and cannot establish biological activity, safety, pharmacokinetics, or clinical success.

faq.question: Can I use custom property thresholds?
faq.answer: Yes. You can set ranges or limits for molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen bonding, and rotatable bonds.

faq.question: Does the script modify my input file?
faq.answer: No. It reads the input and writes results to the requested output path, with an optional summary beside it.
